archetypes.name: arch-consistency
archetypes.rationale: The diff introduces a new immediate-background pattern across multiple interrelated call sites; the most likely defect is an inconsistency in the resume fence contract or a remaining direct-invocation path that bypasses the new wrapper indirection.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine every callsite in skills/design/SKILL.md and skills/implement/SKILL.md that previously invoked run-step3-review.sh or run-step-checks.sh directly to confirm none still call those scripts outside the new wrapper or backgrounded fence. Check that every mid-loop return status enumerated in the post-loop branch matrix (main-agent-vote-required, main-agent-apply-required, per-round-approval-required, postplan-operator-required) uses the Step 3 resume fence and NOT a direct run-step3-review.sh invocation. Verify that the new design-step3-review.sh wrapper correctly handles both the with- and without-starting-round code paths, including the empty-string edge case. Confirm that the anti-halt rule in both SKILL.md files correctly states that for immediate-background fences, the orchestrator must wait for <task-notification> before consuming result files. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: risk-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan explicitly requires inspecting ALL long-running scripts in both skills and backgrounding any that take over 30 seconds, but the diff only converts a specific set; the count-based structural test in test-implement-structure.sh uses a magic number without anchoring it to an enumerated list of backgrounded sites.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the diff has addressed all long-running scripts called from both /design and /implement skills, not just the handful explicitly converted. In particular check whether run-step5-review.sh, step-7a.sh, step-8-ship.sh, and ci-wait.sh invocation sites in skills/implement/SKILL.md also carry the immediate-background notice and timeout, since NEVER #8 now claims these should be backgrounded. Inspect the test-implement-structure.sh assertion that skill_text.count('timeout: 10800000') < 4 is a hard gate: determine if 4 is the correct expected minimum count by tallying all backgrounded run-step-checks.sh call sites in the current SKILL.md, and flag if the threshold is wrong or untethered to an enumerated list. Check whether design-step-final-summary.sh and design-step5c.sh being backgrounded (21600000 timeout) could cause the orchestrator to incorrectly proceed to step 5d or step 6 before their notifications fire. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
